newsitem.title: USA: Norfolk Southern sets record $4.3 bln debt deal.
newsitem.headline: Norfolk Southern sets record $4.3 bln debt deal.

text.p: Norfolk Southern Corp issued $4.3 billion in an eight-part debt offering via joint lead managers JP Morgan Securities and Merrill Lynch & Co Inc on Wednesday, sources said.
The deal was deemed the largest ever investment grade offering in corporate bond history, according to research firm Securities Data Co.
Securities Data said prior to Norfolk Southern's deal, the record was held by U S West Inc, which sold $4.1 billion in investment grade debt in January of this year.
Norfolk Southern's Baa1/BBB-plus rated deal consists of the following eight tranches, according to sources.
-- $400 million in 6.70 percent notes due May 1, 2000 priced at 99.873 to yield 6.75 percent, at 36 basis points over Treasuries.
-- $200 million in 6.875 percent notes due May 1, 2001 priced at 99.913 to yield 6.902 percent, at 39 basis points over Treasuries.
-- $500 million in 6.95 percent notes due May 1, 2002 priced at 99.848 to yield 6.988 percent, at 45 basis points over Treasuries.
-- $750 million in 7.05 percent notes due May 1, 2037, putable in the seventh year, at 99.886 to yield 7.072 percent at +43 basis points.
-- $750 million in 7.35 percent notes due May 15, 2007, at 99.931 to yield 7.36 percent at +67 basis points.
-- $550 million in 7.70 percent bonds due May 15, 2017 at 99.890 to yield 7.711 percent at +77 basis points.
-- $800 million in 7.80 percent bonds due May 15, 2027 at 99.874 to yield 7.811 percent at +87 basis points.
-- $350 million in 7.90 percent bonds due May 15, 2097 at 99.863 to yield 7.911 at +97 basis points.
The three-year, four-year, five-year and 10-year tranches are non-callable for life.
The 20-year, 30-year, 40-year put-seven and 100-year bond have make-whole-call features at +20 over U.S. Treasuries.
The 20-year, 30-year and 100-year tranches were priced at a spread over the old U.S. Treasury 30-year bond.
Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette Securities and PaineWebber Inc were co-managers on the offering.
The net proceeds from the offering will be used to finance Norfolk Southern's proposed acquisition of 58 percent of the assets of Conrail Inc for $6 billion.
